objective_for_doctor: A 0-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have weakness in both arms and/or both legs, significant dyspnea, and foot numbness/tingling.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’m having weakness in both my arms and legs, and I also feel numbness and tingling in my feet. I’ve had significant trouble breathing, and I recently also had numbness/tingling around my mouth and in both arms and legs.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—this sounds urgent; do you have trouble swallowing or speaking, and are these symptoms sudden (minutes–hours) or gradual (days–weeks)?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any fever, recent infection or vaccination, or new medications, and is your breathing worse when lying flat?

Doctor, I don’t know about trouble swallowing or speaking—I haven’t noticed that. The symptoms started and got worse after my recent viral infection, so it feels more gradual over days rather than suddenly within minutes to hours. I did have a viral infection recently, and my breathing feels bad overall, but I’m not sure about whether it’s worse when I lie flat.

Doctor: I’m concerned about a post-viral neurologic cause—any facial weakness, double vision, or trouble keeping your eyes open, and have you had worsening weakness that’s symmetrical and moving up your body?  
Doctor: Also, can you tell me: do you have decreased reflexes, and are you able to walk normally or is it progressively harder over the last few days?

I think the numbness/tingling was also around my mouth, but I don’t think I have facial weakness. I don’t have double vision or trouble keeping my eyes open.  

My weakness has been getting worse over the last few days and it feels symmetrical in both arms and legs, and my walking is getting harder. I don’t know about reflexes.

Doctor: I’m going to examine you—can you briefly tell me if your reflexes feel normal or decreased (quick knee-jerk/ankle-jerk), and do you have new bladder/bowel problems or numbness that’s spreading upward?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_and_Spine (urgent) AND REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture_with_CSF_analysis (if safe) AND REQUEST TEST: EMG_NCS

I’m not sure about my reflexes—I haven’t checked my knee-jerk or ankle-jerk myself. I don’t have new bladder or bowel problems that I’ve noticed. The numbness/tingling feels like it’s in my feet and also in both arms and around my mouth, and it seems to be spreading/worsening over the last few days.

Doctor: This combination—rapidly progressive, symmetrical arm/leg weakness after a viral illness plus tingling around the mouth, and significant dyspnea—most strongly suggests an acute peripheral nerve disorder; I need to check for breathing/nerve involvement urgently: are you able to swallow normally and speak without getting short of breath, and do you have facial weakness at all?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary_Function_Tests (FVC/NIF) now, AND REQUEST TEST: Bedside_Strength_and_Reflexes (knee-jerk/ankle-jerk, facial/eye exam), AND REQUEST TEST: CT_Head_or_Cervical_Spine (if any red flags)
I can’t really say about swallowing—I haven’t noticed it getting worse, but I’m not fully sure. Speaking makes me feel short of breath. I don’t think I have facial weakness.

Doctor: Given you feel short of breath while speaking and you have rapidly progressive, symmetrical limb weakness with perioral tingling after a viral illness, I’m worried about **Guillain-Barré syndrome with possible respiratory/neuromuscular weakness**—we must assess urgently: can you take a deep breath and hold it for 10 seconds, and do you feel worse when trying to breathe out forcefully?  
Doctor: Also, are you having any trouble with eye movements, facial numbness/weakness, or any new severe back/neck pain?

I can try, but I feel like I get short of breath quickly, so holding my breath for 10 seconds is hard. I can’t say about whether it’s worse when breathing out forcefully.  

I don’t have trouble with eye movements, and I don’t have new severe back or neck pain. I did have tingling around my mouth, but I don’t think my face is weak.

Doctor: I need a quick neurologic and respiratory check—on a scale of 0–10, how bad is your shortness of breath at rest, and are you able to count to 20 out loud on one breath?  
Doctor: Also, have you noticed new facial weakness, trouble swallowing liquids, or that you can’t lift your head well against gravity?

At rest, my shortness of breath feels about a 7 out of 10. I can’t count to 20 on one breath.  

I haven’t noticed facial weakness, and I don’t think I have trouble swallowing liquids. I also can’t really tell about lifting my head against gravity.

Doctor: This is an emergency—your dyspnea at rest (7/10) and inability to count to 20 on one breath strongly suggest respiratory muscle involvement from a likely acute neuromuscular process (most concerning for Guillain-Barré). REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Bedside_Respiratory_Measures (NIF, FVC) NOW AND REQUEST TEST: ABG_VBG; also I’m asking: do you have escalating difficulty breathing when lying flat or do you need to sit upright to breathe?  
Doctor: If you confirm you need to sit upright to breathe, I will proceed as if airway/respiratory failure risk is imminent—are you currently able to swallow your saliva/clear secretions, and do you have any choking or pooling of saliva?
I need to sit upright to breathe—I get worse when I lie flat. I think I can swallow my saliva and clear my secretions, and I don’t feel like I’m choking or pooling saliva.

Doctor: This is an emergency consistent with **Guillain-Barré syndrome with respiratory muscle weakness**; I’m going to treat this as high risk for impending respiratory failure—are you currently receiving oxygen, and has anyone called EMS or transferred you to the ICU?  
Doctor: I’m also placing a request for immediate **REQUEST TEST: ICU_Immediate_Respiratory_Monitoring (continuous pulse oximetry, serial FVC/NIF)**; while we do that, do you have any history of blood clots, severe asthma, or heart failure that could worsen dyspnea?

I’m not sure if I’m receiving oxygen yet. I haven’t been transferred to ICU, but I think the team is taking it seriously.  

I don’t have a history of blood clots, severe asthma, or heart failure that I know of.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given your rapidly progressive weakness after a viral illness, perioral/limb tingling, and inability to count on one breath (plus worse lying flat), this is an emergency consistent with **Guillain-Barré syndrome with respiratory muscle weakness**; we must act now—are you in a hospital/ED right now with staff actively monitoring your breathing and measuring NIF/FVC?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Immediate_NIF_and_FVC_and_Serial_Measurements (q4-6h or per protocol) AND REQUEST TEST: Continuous_Pulse_Oximetry_with_Cardiac_Monitoring AND REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas (ABG) NOW.
Yes, I’m in the ED right now, and the staff are actively checking me and monitoring my breathing. They haven’t told me the exact NIF/FVC numbers yet, but they’re taking it seriously.

Doctor: I want to narrow the cause—did your viral illness come about 1–4 weeks before weakness started, and have you had any severe diarrhea (especially in the weeks before), fever, or recent surgery?  
Doctor: Also, are you having numbness that’s more prominent than weakness (sensory loss), and do you notice decreased or absent reflexes on exam in the ED?

Yes, the viral illness was about 1–4 weeks before the weakness started. I don’t think I had severe diarrhea, and I didn’t have recent surgery.  

I think the weakness is the main problem, but I do have tingling/numbness too—especially in my feet and around my mouth. I don’t know about my reflexes because I haven’t been told what they are on exam.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Guillain-Barré syndrome (post-viral immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy) with respiratory muscle weakness causing significant dyspnea.

[DDX]
1. Guillain-Barré syndrome
